Ashley (support): Hey team, getting a customer escalation — multiple 502s from hosted inference API since ~09:15 PST. Ticket C-1092. Customer seeing timeouts + billing noise. Anyone triaging?
Ops Bot: ALERT: hosted-api.gateway returned 502 spike at 2026-03-17T09:16:12Z -> control-plane dep failures (auth/session, routing-policy). 100+ 5xx in last 5m. Paging oncall.
Mia Chen: I see the same in logs. Correlation: control-plane routing-policy svc returning 5xx, and a bunch of configdb timeouts right before.
Sanjay Kapoor: grabbing routing-policy logs now. Initial suspicion: configdb connection pool exhausted -> routing-policy hits 500 when trying to read tenant rules.
Luke Rivera: Can you paste a sample stack/log?
Sanjay Kapoor: Paste: ```
2026-03-17T09:15:58Z ERROR routing-policy [tenant=acme] fetchRules err=timeout "dial tcp 10.3.5.12:5432: i/o timeout" src=node-3
2026-03-17T09:16:01Z WARN routing-policy pool_active=102 pool_max=100
2026-03-17T09:16:03Z ERROR routing-policy upstream=controlplane auth/session: 502 returned
```
Ashley (support): Customer also noted higher token billing count because clients retried. They're asking for repro steps and ETA.
Mia Chen: Repro: run this locally against staging to simulate connections: ```for i in {1..200}; do curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://hosted-api.redwood.example/v1/generate & done``` watch for 502s and PG pool metrics.
Luke Rivera: Temporary mitigations we can push now: 1) enable routing-policy fallback to cached-default (fast config) 2) add a short lived circuit-breaker to upstream calls to configdb 3) scale configdb read replicas + increase pool size.
Oncall Eng: I can push a routing-policy feature flag to enable fallback, rolling now. ETA 7m. Also opening an incident page.
Ops Bot: ACTION: feature-flag rollout started by Oncall Eng -> routing.policy.fallback=true on prod-0.
Sanjay Kapoor: After enabling fallback, 502s drop significantly in the gateway. We're still seeing some auth/session 5xx from nodes that caught errors during the spike (stale sessions).
Mia Chen: Added a short auth-session-cache purge job to clear stuck sessions for tenants with errors. Command: `kubectl exec -n controlplane deploy/auth-service -- /bin/purge-stale-sessions --tenant acme` (ran for affected tenants).
Ashley (support): I told customer a tactical workaround (retries with jitter and exponential backoff, and ask customers to retry after 30s), and that we're doing an infra mitigation. Customer asked for RCA and timeline.
Sanjay Kapoor: Root cause so far: routing-policy svc overwhelmed by sudden surge of read requests after a config change + configdb connection pool mis-sizing. The pool did not reject gracefully -> cascading 5xx to routing-policy -> gateway.
Luke Rivera: Planned fix: 1) increase configdb pool size to 250 for routing-policy, 2) harden retry/backoff in routing-policy to avoid tight loops, 3) add circuit-breaker and local cached fallback for 30s, 4) add alerting for pool_active > 80%. Will create PRs and a rollout plan.
Oncall Eng: Filed incident INC-2026-0317-1, assigned to eng-infra and eng-platform. ETA for stable rollouts ~3h for config change + controlled release.
Ashley (support): Customer updated: "thanks, please keep us posted. We saw reduced errors after your flags."
Mia Chen: Postmortem note to include: reproducer script, affected tenants list, exact timestamps, telemetry screenshots, and the config change that precipitated the surge.
Sanjay Kapoor: Follow-up: After pool bump + fallback flag, observed normal rates and CPU back to baseline. No further billing anomalies reported yet; support will follow up with customer billing if needed.
Luke Rivera: I'll open a tracking issue and link to PRs. Also adding a small test in e2e to simulate configdb saturation.
Ashley (support): Closing the customer ticket with status "mitigated, monitoring" and linking incident. Will re-open if errors reoccur. Thanks everyone :heart:
Oncall Eng: Incident moved to postmortem state. Marking as resolved for now.
